holidays.name: National Sticky Bun Day
holidays.description: A gooey, swirly, caramel-drenched celebration of the pastry that glues your fingers together and your heart to the breakfast table. Pecans, cinnamon and butter are all welcome. Napkins are strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. The treat itself is tied to German immigrants in Pennsylvania, whose cinnamon snail-shaped buns (schnecken) grew into the sticky bun Americans know today.
holidays.funFact: Sticky buns are baked upside down. The sugary, buttery glaze pools at the bottom of the pan, and the buns are flipped out so it drips down over the top.

holidays.name: Card Reading Day
holidays.description: A day for turning over cards and seeing what they have to say. Tarot, oracle decks and other card readings all fit the occasion. Pull a card, ponder the message and make up your own mind about it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with card readers and fans of divination and mysticism.
holidays.funFact: The earliest tarot decks, from 15th-century Italy, were made for a trick-taking card game called tarocchi. Their use for fortune-telling came later.

holidays.name: International Mother Language Day
holidays.description: A worldwide celebration of linguistic diversity, from widely spoken tongues to those with only a few speakers left. It is a day to tell stories, share words and phrases, and protect the languages that carry cultures' jokes, songs and memories.
holidays.origin: UNESCO proclaimed the day in 1999, and it has been observed worldwide since 2000. It honors the Language Movement in Dhaka, Bangladesh, where students protesting for recognition of the Bengali language were killed on February 21, 1952.
holidays.funFact: The day was proposed by Bangladesh. It is a rare international observance that began as a tribute to a student-led protest.
